touches.text: Akien 2026-11-13, said in akiendell's session, answering the same Q#93 on a second asking (verbatim): "no there's no conflict there. those are completely different kinds of things. spinning up a second ground loop should see the first, and that it's fine, and exit quietly. if we're starting a new one on purpose, like there's an older one running, we'll add --force, which means kill the old one. we change that intention. i have no recollection why it says loudly. but the naming, yes. if we had two zeros how would messages get routed? or <host>_cc_RESCUE? we DO want to be able to spin up more than one of something. many things can be singletons or not... like the embeddings generator. if we wound up with too much traffic, we might open a second on another host. but the launcher has to ask the shim to create the instance, and so it's the shim's job to say 'we've been asked to start and instance, then we've not been given a name for it, then we have a cc_0 instance, so I'll launch it with cc_1'"

An instance is declared by its folder existing in class-space: cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ (one address in two roots). Declared = the folders (read by the rack tool, 17.20); running = which of those are in the rack.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
